newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korea's Hanbo Eng defaults on promissory notes.
newsitem.headline: S.Korea's Hanbo Eng defaults on promissory notes.

text.p: Hanbo Engineering and Construction Co, an unlisted affiliate of the troubled Hanbo Group, defaulted on promissory notes on Thursday, the company's main creditor Korea First Bank said on Friday.
"Hanbo was unable to honour 6.5 billion won worth of promissory notes on maturity," a Korea First official said.
The Hanbo Group has been in trouble after its flagship, Hanbo Steel Co, was declared insolvent in late January under $5.8 billion in debts.
Hanbo Steel, South Korea's second-largest steel maker, has been seeking court receivership.

The collapse of Hanbo uncovered a poor system of credit analysis and corrupt lending practices and sparked a bribes-for-loans scandal that has put three top bankers and several of President Kim Young-sam's closest aides on trial.
It also shook the stock and money markets on fears of a domino effect of corporate failures.
